title: Telemetry eraser: backpressure, verifiable deletion, and consumer-safe replay
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a resilient Telemetry Eraser service for console analytics that accepts user deletion/retention workflows and enforces them across streaming and batch consumers. The service must: 1) accept deletion/retention requests (user/organization-level and event-level), 2) coordinate safe removal or redaction from live streaming pipelines and materialized analytics stores, 3) provide verifiable deletion receipts customers can use for compliance, and 4) avoid wide regressions in ingestion throughput by applying backpressure and graceful degradation policies.
acceptance_criteria: API to submit deletion requests with scoping (org, project, session, event id) and TTL is available
Deletion requests produce deletion-tombstone markers to streaming topics and a durable ledger entry within 30s
Backpressure signal prevents unbounded memory growth when deletion backlog > configured threshold and falls back to soft-erase policy
Signed deletion receipts available for completed scopes and introspectable from the Console within 24h
End-to-end integration test covers streaming replay, tombstone compaction, and verification step
Dashboard shows deletion backlog, throughput impact, and proof generation latency with alerts
tasks: Design API contract and data model for deletion requests (proto + REST)
Add durable ledger table (append-only) to store deletion intents and generation status
Emit tombstone markers to analytics topics with opaque deletion-token headers
Implement consumer-side adapters to honor tombstones and ack deletion-token consumption
Build backpressure controller based on consumer-lag and tombstone-queue-length metrics
Integrate with KMS for signing deletion receipts and rotate signing keys via existing key service
Create canary job and end-to-end test harness using a trimmed dataset
Add console UI elements and API surface for customers to request receipts and check status
Run privacy/security review and update runbook for major deletion incidents
implementation_notes: We will implement tombstones as lightweight messages with a stable deletion-token header so consumers can do idempotent delete/redact. To avoid blocking ingestion, the eraser will not synchronously wait for every downstream consumer; instead it will record intent in the ledger and track consumer ack progress via offsets. If the backlog exceeds safety thresholds, the backpressure controller will start shedding non-critical low-priority telemetry and switch to a soft-erase mode (redact fields at the materialization layer) while continuing to drive hard deletions asynchronously. Deletion receipts are short JSON blobs signed by the cluster KMS; they include ledger entry id, scope, timestamp, and a Merkle-like subtree hash for the affected partition. We scoped out full cryptographic shredding in this ticket because it requires offline-compaction work and disk-level key rotation (follow-up ticket planned).
decisions: Prefer append-only ledger + async tombstone fanout over synchronous blocking of producers
Use signing receipts (KMS) for proof-of-deletion rather than immediate crypto-shred to keep initial latency low
Expose conservative backpressure thresholds by default and allow customer config on Dedicated/Private tiers
Consumers must expose an ack endpoint (or use committed offsets) for the eraser to mark progress; bridges will be provided for older consumers

notes_on_tradeoffs: We accepted eventual consistency for downstream deletion confirmation to keep ingest latency predictable. This means receipts are only issued when the ledger shows consumer ack progress past configured fences; customers that require immediate physical disk shredding will need Private deployment add-on and a separate crypto-shred flow. Backpressure mitigates unbounded resource usage but introduces potential telemetry loss for low-priority events — documented in the runbook and opt-in configurable per-tenant.
